summary: This work demonstrates that restricting noise bias to ancilla qubits in syndrome extraction circuits can significantly improve the performance of quantum low-density parity-check codes without requiring code tailoring or bias-preserving CX gates. For the [[144,12,12]] bicycle bivariate code at circuit noise $p = 2 	imes 10^{-3}$ with ancilla bit-flip suppression $	imes 50$, ancilla-only biased noise achieves an 8.5-fold reduction in logical error rate compared to depolarizing noise, primarily through elimination of hook errors and reduction of short cycles in the Tanner graph.
motivation: Standard syndrome extraction for QLDPC codes suffers from hook errors (ancilla faults propagating to multiple data qubits) that reduce circuit-level distance and from short loops in the Tanner graph that impair belief propagation decoding. Previous biased-noise QEC schemes required difficult-to-implement bias-preserving CX gates or code redesign.
method: We simulated circuit-level memory storage using three instances of bicycle bivariate codes ([[72,12,6]], [[90,8,10]], [[144,12,12]]) and the [[336,20,6]] cyclic hypergraph product code under four noise models: depolarizing, ancilla-only biased ($	ext{BIAS}_2[	au, p]$ on ancilla-controlled gates), non-CX biased (CZ-preserving bias without bias-preserving CX), and full-bias (Z-errors only). We quantified hook errors via circuit-level distance bounds and counted 4- and 6-cycles in detector error model Tanner graphs, then compared logical error rates using BP+OSD-CS-7 decoding with joint X-Z syndrome decoding.
result: At $	au = 100$ and $p = 2 	imes 10^{-3}$, the [[144,12,12]] code with ancilla-only biased noise achieved 8.5-fold logical error rate reduction versus depolarizing noise; the [[336,20,6]] HGP code achieved 4.2-fold reduction. Circuit-level distance was restored from 10 to 12 for the [[90,8,10]] code under biased ancilla. Short 4-cycles and 6-cycles were reduced by orders of magnitude: for the gross code, 4-cycles dropped from 12.5M (depolarizing) to 1.2M (ancilla-only bias) to 79k (full-bias).
